There actually are some differences, but not necessarily in terms of average intelligence. To put it in statistical terms, the distribution of post-pubescent male intelligence is much larger than that of post-pubescent female intelligence. In other words, statistically speaking, if you were to look for a person with an extremely low IQ, they would most likely be male. If you were looking for someone with an extremely high IQ, they would also most likely be male. If you were looking for someone with an average IQ (average IQ is, by definition, 100), they would most likely be female. But even this depends on which tests and metrics you use. For more information, this wikipedia section does a decent job: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_differences_in_intelligence

STOCKHOLM – Swedish citizens are out in full force today to elect a new Riksdag and Prime minister. This election promises to be one of the most controversial in recent times with the rise of the far-right Social Democrats party which remains neck and neck in the polls with the Social Democratic party and Moderate Party.

The Social Democratic Party (S) is the largest political party in the Swedish Riksdag with 113 of the 349 seats, it represents the centre-left and follows the ideologies of social democracy. The party supports egalitarianism, social welfare provision paid for from progressive taxation, and maintain a strong opposition to discrimination and racism. The Social Democratic Party is the major component of the incumbent Löfven Cabinet along the Green Party. Its current party leader Stefan Löfven has been Prime Minister of Sweden since 3 October 2014, and seeks to continue his Löfven Cabinet.

The Moderate Party (M) is the second-largest party in the Riksdag with 84 seats, it follows ideologies of Liberal conservatism and represents the centre-right. Past policies include the campaigning for the adoption of the Euro, and Swedish membership in NATO. They lead the initiative for the 2017 admission of Sweden into the Nordic Union. It was the largest governing party under Prime Minister Fredrik Reinfeldt from 2006 to 2014. Anna Kinberg Batra became party leader on 10 January 2015, her party is involved in the Alliance alongside three other parties, which will seek to return to power together.

The Sweden Democrats (SD) is the third-largest party in the Riksdag with 49 seats, it represents the far-right and follows ideologies of Swedish Nationalism. Their platform includes reevaluating Sweden’s relationship with the EU, seeking further immigration restrictions and supporting the funding for “traditional Swedish culture” over multiculturalism. Their growing support is the reason for Sweden placing immigration restrictions in 2017. In the 2014 general election the party increased its share of seats by 29, becoming the third-largest party. The party leader is Jimmie Åkesson. The other Riksdag parties have repeatedly stated that they will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats in a future government.
